title: A milestone's own description claims a PR shipped that never merged
author: off-by-one
description: Extracts every ships/includes/merges/via #N PR-claim phrase (pr_claims.py's shared grammar) from a milestone's own description and cross-checks it against the live PR tracker's own state. A PR that exists but never merged is the seam: a milestone's own permanent description already disagrees with GitHub's own record, and nothing on GitHub's side ever compares the two. The missing milestone-side leg of the claims-unmerged-pr family alongside readme-claims-unmerged-pr, release-claims-unmerged-pr, tweet-claims-unmerged-pr, and mention-claims-unmerged-pr -- all four already covered a text surface either the town itself controls or a stranger's own inbound mention; this one closes the one remaining surface none of them ever read, the same milestone-side leg milestone-claims-unfixed-issue (task 535) already opened for the sibling claims-unfixed-issue family.
confidence_notes: Age-gated off the milestone's own updated_at, holding milestone-claims-unfixed-issue's own 0.55/0.85 bar exactly -- 0.55 within 24h since last update (may not have merged yet), 0.85 past it (nobody is coming back for it). A milestone description, like an issue or PR body, is a text surface its author can edit at any time, so a fresh false claim earns a grace period before being scored as a confirmed gap -- deliberately not a flat score like readme-claims-unmerged-pr's own live-read reasoning. A claimed PR that doesn't exist at all is excluded here, named not hidden -- that broken reference is milestone-body-dangling-reference's own seam. A claimed PR that IS merged is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. A milestone with no description at all is excluded outright -- there is no claim to have broken.
